title: Pressurised sphere, axisymmetric Reissner-Mindlin ring element vs thin-shell membrane solution
generated_by: benchmarks/verified/fem_sphere_pressure_membrane/emit_certificate.py (derived from benchmarks/verified/fem_sphere_pressure_membrane/result.json; zero solve, zero hand-typed number)

gates.quantity: max over Gauss points of |sigma_theta/(pR/2t) - 1|, 8 facets (27 dof)
gates.note: hoop stress; max over the raw Gauss-point set stored in result.json

gates.quantity: max over Gauss points of |sigma_phi/(pR/2t) - 1|, 8 facets
gates.note: meridional stress, independent Gauss-point set from G1

gates.reference: the membrane state of a pressurised sphere is equi-biaxial
gates.note: membrane-force anisotropy; a sphere has no preferred meridional direction
displacement is nu-dependent, so this gate also exercises nu

gates.quantity: e(8)/e(4), e = max Gauss sigma_theta rel. error
gates.reference: error must contract under refinement: e(4) > e(8)
gates.note: scalarised member 1 of the legacy vector gate G5_monotone_refinement

gates.quantity: e(32)/e(8), e = max Gauss sigma_theta rel. error
gates.reference: error must contract under refinement: e(8) > e(32)
gates.note: scalarised member 2 of the legacy vector gate G5_monotone_refinement

gates.quantity: min observed log-log order of the sigma_theta ladder (2..64 facets)
gates.reference: > 1.5 rules out a merely consistent (order 1) element
gates.note: full ladder [3.456, 3.948, 3.989, 4.025, 3.48]; the minimum is the binding member

gates.quantity: max over nu in {0,0.2,0.3,0.4,0.49} of the sigma_theta rel. error
gates.reference: closed-sphere membrane stress does not depend on nu
gates.note: w would move with nu; the stress must not

gates.reference: the thin-shell formula must itself be within tolerance of 3-D elasticity at the case point
gates.note: validates the reference used by G1-G4, not the element

gates.reference: control must MISS the tolerance: geometry representation matters, the element does not rescue it
gates.note: same element, same mesh, only the circular meridian switched off

gates.quantity: N_mean rel. error of the merged flat-facet Shell4 path, 24 facets
gates.reference: control must MISS the tolerance by orders of magnitude
gates.note: independent element on the same case; reproduces the recorded 13316.6 % (recorded source: 'docs/sphere-membrane-validation.md section 3')

predictions.statement: the thin-shell reference stays within tolerance up to t/R = 0.05
predictions.note: falsified prediction kept in the record: the band ends near t/R = 0.02 and the thin-vs-Lame deviation scales linearly in t/R (slope 1.0276), so the reference cannot reach 0.05 within a 3 % tolerance

limitations: Thin-shell (Reissner-Mindlin) theory only: the case grades the element against *shell* theory, and the shell formula's own distance from 3-D elasticity is measured separately by G8a (+4.013e-01 % at t/R = 0.004).
Uniform internal pressure on a closed spherical shell only: no boundary layers, no edge loads, no external restraint, and no bending-dominated state is exercised.

The certificate figures are rendered on demand by build_report.py into artifacts/ and are not committed, so the certificate declares no figure artifact (declaring an uncommitted path would be an E_ARTIFACT_MISSING defect).
G9 and G10 are negative controls: they pass when the control *misses* the tolerance, so a passing certificate is not evidence that every geometric representation of the meridian works.
